D015_m001.question:
I’ve been feelin’ off for over a year now—like, really off. At first, I thought it was just work stress or being tired. I’m a plumber, been doin’ it 15 years, used to take pride in fixin’ things, showin’ up early, gettin’ the job done right. But now? Doesn’t matter. I finish a job, customer thanks me, and I just… nod. Don’t feel nothin’. Like my chest is full of concrete.

My head’s always foggy, like I’m underwater. I forget tools, mess up simple fittings. My wife notices. She asks if I’m okay, but I don’t know how to tell her I don’t even care about things I used to. Even my kid’s soccer games—I sit there, but I’m not really *there*.

Last few months, it’s gotten worse. I’ll be alone in the van between jobs and see shadows moving in the back alleyways—figures watchin’ me. I know it ain’t right, but I swear they’re followin’ me. Government vans, plainclothes guys in parking lots. They know things. They’re recording me somehow.

And honestly? Some mornings, I just wish I wouldn’t wake up. Not that I’d do anything—but it’d be easier. Like the world wouldn’t miss me anyway.
D015_m001.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m001.answer: A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m002.question:
I’ve felt like I’m moving through fog for over a year now. Everything’s heavy—my chest, my thoughts, even opening my eyes in the morning. I don’t enjoy my work anymore, even though I used to love designing interfaces. Now I just sit at my desk, staring at the screen, unable to care if it looks good or not. My husband keeps saying I’m pulling away, but I can’t help it. I miss the person I was, but she feels like a stranger now.

Lately… it’s been worse. I keep hearing my phone buzz, but there’s no message—except the voice. It whispers things, like he’s cheating on me. I know it doesn’t make sense—there’s no proof—but I *feel* it. Like I can *hear* her laughing when he’s on a call, even though he’s just talking to his mom. I tried recording one of those voices once… but there was nothing. Still, I can't shake it.

I haven’t told anyone. A few months ago, I took a whole bottle of sleeping pills. It wasn’t serious, I guess—I called my husband before I passed out. But I’m tired. Not just sleepy—tired of feeling like I’m broken, like my mind is lying to me while I drown slowly in silence.
D015_m002.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m002.answer: A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m003.question:
I’ve been feeling this way for over a year now—since not long after my wife passed. It’s just me in the house now, and the days blend together. I used to enjoy driving the kids in the morning, but now I don’t even care. Some days I sit in the bus with the engine off for an extra ten minutes just trying to make myself start the route. I cry at the littlest things—during the quiet drives, when a kid reminds me of my own son growing up. I can’t even decide what to eat most days. Picking clothes? Forget it. Sometimes I just stand in front of the closet like it’s a wall.

Lately, things have gotten… strange. I keep smelling cigarette smoke in the bus, but no one’s been on it, and I don’t smoke. It’s sharp, like burnt matches. I know it’s not real, but it’s there every few days. And sometimes I get the strong feeling that people are watching me—cameras in the mirrors, someone reporting my mistakes. School admin, maybe, or even the parents. Like they’re waiting for me to mess up so they can take me off the road.

I think about dying sometimes—not how, just… it’d be easier. Like sinking into deep water and not having to come up.
D015_m003.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m003.answer: A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m004.question:
It’s been over a year now—maybe a little more—since I first started feeling like I was losing my grip. At first, it was just the sadness. I’d sit in my office at the museum, surrounded by artifacts that used to fascinate me, and I couldn’t care less. I curated a new exhibit last fall, something I would’ve been proud of once, but it felt meaningless. I didn’t even notice when the director praised it.  

The tears come out of nowhere. I’ll be reviewing inventory or responding to emails, and suddenly I’m sobbing at my desk. Thinking has become so hard—like my mind is wrapped in thick gauze. I can’t focus, and decisions exhaust me.  

But then… the other things started. I became certain the world is ending—that everything we preserve in the museum is pointless because nothing will survive. It’s not a fear. It’s a fact, in my mind. And sometimes, when I’m alone at night, I taste something metallic, like blood, though there’s nothing there. I tasted it yesterday while brushing my teeth.  

About six months ago, I took a bottle of sleeping pills. I don’t want to die, not really, but I just couldn’t bear another day of this. I couldn’t reach anyone in time. I’m… still here. Barely.
D015_m004.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m004.answer: A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m005.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for over a year now—just dragging through each day. I used to take pride in my job, getting people where they needed to go on time, but honestly, nothing feels meaningful anymore. I’ll be driving and suddenly realize I don’t care if I get paid or not. I even forget where I parked the car sometimes, or if I turned off the meter. That never used to happen.  

Some days are worse. I hear voices—just low murmurs, like someone’s talking behind a closed door. They say things like, “You’re the chosen one” or “The city runs through you.” Sounds crazy, I know, but it feels real when it happens. Sometimes I even think I can control traffic lights just by looking at them. Like I’ve got some kind of power no one else understands.  

But then… I’ll come down from that, and the weight comes back—the emptiness. I find myself thinking, “Would it just be easier if I wasn’t here?” Not that I’d do anything, but the thought doesn’t go away. My ex-wife says I’ve changed, and she’s right. I can’t keep up with the job, can’t focus. Used to be reliable. Now I’m just… gone.
D015_m005.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m005.answer: A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m006.question:
I’ve been crying a lot—more than I ever have. It just hits me, sometimes when I’m at a red signal, sitting there waiting. I’ll start tearing up and can’t stop, even though I’m in uniform and trying to hold it together. It’s been like this for about four months. Before that, I was fine—regular shifts, kept to myself, didn’t have any big problems.

Lately, I can’t stop thinking about this one mistake I made—back in February, I started braking a second too late at Roosevelt station. No one was hurt, but I keep replaying it, like a tape. I should’ve been perfect. I *should’ve* known better. I even wrote a note—just in case. Took some pills once, but got scared and flushed them.

Now my skin crawls all the time, like something’s moving under it, ants or wires—but no bugs, and the doctors can’t find anything. I asked two different ones. They say my heart, my lungs, everything’s fine, but I *know* something’s wrong inside. I feel it burning in my chest, like my organs are rotting. I can't sleep, can’t focus on the route. I’ve been calling in sick. I don’t trust myself on the tracks anymore.
D015_m006.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m006.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m007.question:
I’ve been carrying this heavy sadness for about four months now—some days it feels like I’m walking through mud, even when I’m preaching. I used to find comfort in scripture, in prayer, but now it’s like God’s silence is shouting. I keep thinking I’ve failed Him… that my doubts have brought disaster on my congregation. I heard about a car accident last week involving a young couple from the community, and I can’t shake the feeling it’s my fault—like my spiritual weakness invited that tragedy.  

Sleep’s been restless. When I close my eyes, I sometimes see figures standing near the foot of the bed—shadowy, like people I should recognize but don’t. And during the day, I’ll catch someone out of the corner of my eye, only to turn and find no one there.  

Worse, I’ve been convinced my wife… she’s been distant, but not because of anything she’s done. I know it sounds irrational, but I’m certain she’s involved with someone else—there are “signs” I can’t explain, messages hidden in small things. I don’t even recognize my own thoughts anymore. Lately, I just think, “Would it be better if I weren’t here?” I don’t want to act on it, but the thought won’t leave.
D015_m007.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m007.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m008.question:
I’ve been going through something I can’t quite explain for about four months now. Honestly, it started creeping in slowly—I’d look at a deal I closed years ago and suddenly fixate on some tiny oversight, like not disclosing a pipe issue fast enough, and spiral into thinking I’ve ruined people’s lives. It’s constant. I lie awake replaying every little mistake, even ones that didn’t matter. My wife says I’m not myself—I don’t laugh, I don’t care about things I used to. It’s like I’m just… hollow. Some mornings, I wish I wouldn’t wake up. Not because I want to do anything drastic—just because the thought of another day feels unbearable.

Lately, it’s gotten stranger. I’ve been smelling something—rotten eggs, or maybe sewage—no one else does. It follows me, even in cars, meetings, my office. And people… I can’t help but feel they’re talking about me. My assistant coughed yesterday, and I’m convinced it was a signal—like she was trying to warn someone. I know how this sounds, but in the moment, it feels undeniable. I used to thrive on closing deals, making decisions fast. Now I can’t even get through an email without feeling like everything’s closing in.
D015_m008.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m008.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m009.question:
I’ve just been crying all the time—over nothing, over everything. It’s been like this for about four months. I can’t stop thinking about all the things I got wrong—as an agent, a mother, a wife. I keep going over every deal I ever lost, every open house that flopped, every time I snapped at my kids. I know it sounds crazy, but I can’t shut it off.  

Things got so bad a few weeks ago… I swallowed a whole bottle of my sleeping pills. I don’t want to die, not really, but I just couldn’t take it anymore. My daughter found me and called 911. Since then, I can’t sleep without feeling like something’s crawling under my skin, like bugs burrowing into my arms. I’ve checked, there’s nothing there, but I *feel* it.  

And… I know this sounds strange, but I’m sure something’s terribly wrong inside me. My organs are rotting, I can feel it. I’ve had multiple scans—doctors say I’m fine—but I *know* they’re missing it. I used to love showing homes, closing deals, but now I can’t get out of bed, can barely answer emails. I’m losing clients, and I don’t even care.
D015_m009.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m009.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m010.question:
I’ve just felt… heavy, for months now—about four of them. Some days, getting out of bed feels impossible, like there’s this weight on my chest. I keep thinking about cases I handled wrong, tiny mistakes—like missing a filing deadline once or not catching a precedent early enough. I replay them over and over, wondering if I’ve ruined someone’s life because of my carelessness. I don’t even care about myself much anymore. Sometimes I think, “Wouldn’t it be easier if I just didn’t wake up?” Nothing else hurts, you know?  

It’s gotten so hard to work. My boss gave me fewer cases, but I still can’t focus. There’s this voice at night, when I’m alone—it tells me my heart is rotting, that it’s black and shriveled inside my chest, even though I feel fine physically. I know that sounds strange, but it feels *real*, like a truth only I can hear. Once, in the shower, I swore I heard a doctor whispering, “Your blood’s poisoned.” I checked with my GP—everything’s normal. But the voice comes back, especially when I'm alone and exhausted. It all makes me feel broken beyond fixing.
D015_m010.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m010.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m011.question:
I’ve just felt... heavy, you know? For about seven months now. It started after a tough quarter at work—deadlines, shipments going sideways, and I couldn’t keep up, even though I used to thrive on that pressure. Lately, I can’t shake this sadness. It’s there when I wake up, before my feet even hit the floor. I lie in bed for hours, mind racing, unable to fall asleep no matter how exhausted I am. By the time I doze off, it’s almost morning.

At work, I’m supposed to be managing teams, coordinating deliveries across three states, but I can barely focus on an email. My brain feels like it’s wading through mud. I’ve missed reports, dropped balls—I’ve never been like this before. My wife keeps asking if something’s wrong, but I don’t want to worry her.

There is... one thing I haven’t told her. I keep getting this feeling—this certainty—that my coworker Sarah, the one in procurement, she’s been sending me signals. Smiling just a little too long, leaving notes in my inbox that feel… coded. I know it sounds off, but I think she’s trying to tell me she loves me, that we’re meant to be together. I don’t talk to her about it, but I can feel it. She wouldn’t say it outright, not with everything I’m going through. But I know she sees me. Maybe she’s the only one who does.
D015_m011.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m011.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m012.question:
Lately… honestly, it’s been like I’m moving through water. It started around last fall—so about seven months now—and it hasn’t let up. I wake up after eight hours of sleep and feel just as tired as when I went to bed, like my body’s full of sand. Some days, getting out of bed to get to school feels impossible. I used to love teaching, but now the kids’ faces just blur together. I don’t feel anything—no joy, no frustration, nothing. It’s like I’m watching my life from behind glass.

And then there’s… well, this is going to sound strange. I keep thinking my ex-girlfriend, who I haven’t even spoken to in over a year, is seeing someone new. Not just suspecting—knowing. I can’t explain it, but I *know* she’s with someone, whispering about me, laughing at how I still care. I’ve seen her in crowds sometimes—once outside the grocery store, another time in the school parking lot—but when I look again, she’s gone. I know it doesn’t make sense, but the feeling is so real. I don’t know what’s wrong with me. I can’t teach like this anymore. I’m scared I’m losing my mind.
D015_m012.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m012.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m013.question:
I’ve just been... empty, really. For about seven months now, it’s like everything’s muffled—happy stuff, sad stuff, nothing gets through. I used to love working on jobsites, figuring out the wiring, even the heavy lifting. But now, my head feels so thick, like I’m wading through mud just to think. I’ll stand there, holding a screwdriver, and forget what I’m doing. My foreman’s starting to notice. I’m scared I’m gonna mess up bad or get hurt.  

Sleep’s a mess too. I crawl into bed exhausted, but my mind just... hums. Sometimes it takes hours to shut it off, if it ever really does.  

And then there’s Jess. We’ve been on and off for two years, but lately I’m sure—*sure*—she’s seeing someone else. She’s always texting, laughing at her phone, coming home late saying she was just out with friends. It doesn’t add up. I’ve checked her location before, and once I thought I saw a man’s jacket in her car that wasn’t mine. I confronted her, and she looked horrified, said I was losing it. But I know what I saw.  

I don’t tell the crew any of this. They’d think I’m weak or crazy. But some days, I can’t get out of the truck. I just sit there, staring at the same circuit diagram, and nothing clicks anymore.
D015_m013.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m013.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m014.question:
I’ve just been… going through the motions, really. For about seven months now, I can’t remember the last time I actually *felt* anything—happy, sad, it’s all the same. It’s like I’m watching my life from behind glass. I run a design firm—used to thrive on creativity, meetings, client compliments—but now, even picking out a fabric swatch feels impossible. I sleep ten, twelve hours a night and still drag around like I’ve been carrying bricks. I canceled a renovation project last month because I couldn’t get out of bed—my assistant had to call the client.

Lately, things have gotten… strange. I know it sounds odd, but I can’t shake the feeling that people are sending me secret messages. My barista yesterday said, “The usual, I see,” when I ordered my coffee, and I *know* he wasn’t just talking about my drink. It felt like he was hinting that he knows how fake I am—how I’m failing everything. Even traffic signs feel pointed—like they’re meant for me. 

I used to pride myself on being sharp, in control. Now I can’t trust my own mind.
D015_m014.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m014.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m015.question:
Lately… it’s been really hard to get through the day. This sadness just sits on my chest, like a weight I can’t shake.     B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D015_m016.question:

D015_m017.question:

D015_m018.question:

D015_m019.question:

D015_m020.question:

    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m021.question:

My doctor says it’s not stroke or infection, but I can’t help but think something inside me is rotting. I used to enjoy my coffee, but now it all just… tastes like rust.

    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m041.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m042.question:
I’ve just been... going through the motions, you know? It’s been almost a year since I started feeling this way—like something inside me just shut down. Running the restaurant used to be my passion, but now I can’t even get through a shift without feeling completely drained. I wake up exhausted, even after sleeping. Talking feels hard—like my thoughts are stuck in mud, and my words can’t catch up.

I keep thinking about all the little things I’ve messed up—the times I snapped at my staff, the supplier I forgot to call months ago that might’ve cost us a contract. I replay them over and over. I know they’re small, but they feel enormous.

And lately... it’s like my body’s betraying me. I’m convinced something’s wrong inside—like my organs are rotting, even though the doctors say I’m fine. And sometimes... I smell this awful, sweet stench—like something’s decaying. No one else notices it. I know that sounds strange… but it feels so real. I haven’t told my husband. I’m afraid he’ll think I’m losing my mind. I just can’t keep pretending I’m okay.

D015_m043.question:
I’ve just been… drowning, I guess. For about nine months now, it’s like a fog I can’t shake. I wake up already exhausted, even if I slept. My body feels like it’s made of concrete—getting out of bed, showering, putting on makeup—it all takes so much effort. At work, I’m a matchmaker; I’ve built my life helping couples connect, but lately, I can’t even look at my own husband without feeling like a fraud. I keep going over old mistakes—times I said the wrong thing to a client, moments I wasn’t “perfect” for my husband—and it loops in my head, over and over. I pace in my office, can’t sit still. I pick at my cuticles until they bleed.

And then… there are the voices. They tell me I’m not just good at my job—I’m destined to save thousands of marriages. That I have a divine gift, that I’m chosen. I hear them most at night, whispering, cheering. I know it sounds crazy, but they sound so real. I’ve started to believe I have a power no one else sees. But… I’m also terrified. Because what if I’m not special? What if I’m just broken?

    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D015_m044.question:
I’ve just not been right for about nine months now. Most days, I can’t find the energy to get out of bed, and even when I do, everything feels so heavy—my body, my thoughts. At work, they keep asking me if I’m okay because I’m so slow to answer. I used to keep up with the dishes, but now even scrubbing a pot takes everything out of me. I don’t sleep poorly—I sleep plenty—but I wake up feeling like I’ve not rested at all.  

It’s more than just being tired, though. I feel… punished. Like the world knows what I’ve done. People at the shelter—the ones I serve meals to—they don’t say it, but I can tell they’re talking about me. A man coughed this morning, and I know it meant I’m being judged. And sometimes, when I eat, there’s this bitter taste, like burnt metal, even when the food is plain toast. The doctor said nothing’s wrong with my mouth, but I *know* it’s there.  

I caused this somehow. My husband’s death, the layoffs at the kitchen last year—God’s holding it all against me because of my sins. I didn’t pray enough when he was sick. I should’ve seen it coming. I should’ve stopped it.
D015_m044.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D015_m044.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m045.question:
I’ve just been... off for months—like, almost a year now. I work the night shift at a gas station, mostly alone, and it’s been getting harder to even talk to people. Honestly, doc, I feel heavy all the time. My mind moves slow, like I’m pushing through mud just to answer a simple question. Sometimes I’ll stand there, customer waiting, and I can’t find the words—like my mouth forgot how to work.

I can’t stop thinking I’ve messed everything up. Like, the other day the register was a few bucks short, and even though it wasn’t my fault, I kept thinking I deserved to be punished for it. I haven’t been sleeping right either. When I do eat, everything tastes like ash—like I’m chewing on old batteries, even water.

And… I won’t lie, I’ve been having weird thoughts. I know how it sounds, but I’ve started believing I’m not like other people. Like I was chosen for something huge—maybe to save people, or that I’m connected to some cosmic force. I don’t feel special in a good way, though. It just makes me feel more alone. Like I’m the only one who sees the truth, and everyone else is blind. It’s exhausting just thinking about it.
D015_m045.options:

    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D015_m046.question:
I’ve just been… going through the motions for about ten months now. Work used to be my thing—I’m an IT consultant, so you’re always solving problems, staying sharp—but now I can’t even finish a simple ticket without feeling like it’s pointless. It doesn’t matter how many projects I close; I still feel like a failure. I keep thinking I’ve ruined everything—with my ex, my kid, my career. I don’t deserve to be happy. 

There were times I couldn’t stop crying, even in the car before walking into a client site. A few months back, I took a bunch of pills. Not all at once, but… I kept them in my desk, waiting for the right moment. I don’t even remember why I stopped myself.

And then there’s this weird taste—like metal or burnt plastic—on my tongue, even when I haven’t eaten anything. I know it doesn’t make sense, but it feels so real, like something’s poisoning me slowly. I checked my water, my food—nothing. My last boss said I seemed “off,” and honestly, I’m scared to take on new contracts now. I just can’t trust my own head.

    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D015_m047.question:
I’ve just... shut down over the past ten months. What used to matter—my work, getting things done right, even small wins at the office—none of it touches me anymore. It’s like I’m watching my life through a window. I used to take pride in policy changes I helped implement, but now? Nothing. Just hollow.  

And then there’s the guilt. I know it sounds irrational, but I’m convinced the flood downtown last spring—when the river overflowed and two people died—was my fault. I didn’t release the dam reports on time. The truth is, the system failed, not me… but I feel it deep in my bones that I killed them. That I ruined everything.  

Sometimes, in the corners of my kitchen at night, I see a little girl standing there, soaked and shivering, just staring. I know she’s not real, but I still talk to her, apologize.  

Six weeks ago, I filled a glass with pills from my cabinet. I’d already written my resignation letter and left it on my desk. I just… couldn’t carry the weight anymore.  

Work is slipping. I’ve called in “sick” for weeks straight. My staff covers for me, but I know they’re worried. I can’t keep pretending I’m okay.
D015_m047.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D015_m047.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m048.question:
I’ve been feeling… hollow… for about ten months now. It started slowly—just not caring about things I used to love, like fixing up old cars or even listening to music. I used to take pride in my cab—kept it clean, knew the city like the back of my hand. Now, I barely notice where I'm going. Passengers talk, but their words don’t really sink in. It’s like I’m watching life from behind glass.

I don’t feel sad so much as… nothing. Like my emotions got turned off. Some days, I sit at stoplights and suddenly get this jolt—like I should just swerve into oncoming traffic. Not because I want to die, exactly. More like I don’t matter, and maybe it’d be easier if I just wasn’t here. I know it’s irrational, but the thought hits hard.

Lately, I’ve been smelling something—burnt hair, like someone’s holding a blowtorch to it. It’ll come outta nowhere, inside the cab, no source. I’ve had it checked—the vents, the engine—but nothing. The mechanic looked at me like I was crazy. Sometimes I wonder if I am. But these smells… they feel real. I’ve read online it might be a brain tumor or something, but deep down, I think it’s my mind breaking because I can’t stop feeling like a waste of space.
D015_m048.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D015_m048.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m049.question:
I’ve just been feeling… empty, for no good reason. It’s been like this for about ten months now. I’m a civil engineer—always prided myself on precision, on being reliable—but lately I can’t focus on the simplest calculations. I don’t enjoy my work anymore, not even weekend drives with my wife like we used to. Nothing feels right. I wake up tired, like the day’s already lost.

There’s this voice, sometimes, when I’m lying in bed at night. It’s not loud, but clear—like someone standing in the room saying, “You’ve failed them all.” I know it’s not real, but it feels true. I keep thinking about all the projects I’ve worked on, bridges, drainage systems… and I get this overwhelming sense that somewhere, something collapsed because of me, even if there’s no proof. Like I caused accidents miles away just by not being perfect.

I don’t want to hurt myself, no plan or anything, but I do catch myself hoping I don’t wake up. It’s exhausting—like I’m dragging the weight of things I didn’t even do. My wife says I’ve changed. I know I have. I just don’t know how to stop the voice… or the guilt.

    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015_m050.question:
I’ve been feelin’ off for about ten months now—like clockwork, right after a job went bad where a pipe burst and flooded an old couple’s basement. I couldn’t stop replaying it, even though it wasn’t really my fault. Lately, nothing feels real. My wife tries to talk to me, hugs me, but I can’t feel anything—not love, not joy, nothing. It’s like I’m numb inside. The things I used to enjoy, like grillin’ out with the kids or fixing up my truck, just don’t matter anymore.

And there’s… stuff I see. Shadows mostly, but sometimes full people—like that couple from the basement, standin’ at the foot of the bed at night, soaked, just *staring*. I know they’re not really there, but it feels like they are. I even apologized to them once, out loud. My wife heard me. That’s when I knew something was really wrong.

I keep thinkin’ I ruined more than just their home—that my messing up caused the husband’s heart attack a few weeks later. I know that sounds crazy, but it feels true in my bones. Last month, I took a handful of pills, just to stop the thoughts. Didn’t tell my wife. I didn’t want her to see me like this. I can’t work right anymore. I’m scared all the time.
D015_m050.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
